content:
Take this free CAT Time and Work online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Time & Work chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Time & Work tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Time & Work

Work rates, combined work, efficiency comparison, pipes and cisterns, and wages in proportion to work done.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • If A finishes in a days, A’s one-day work = 1/a.
  • Together A and B take ab/(a+b) days.
  • Work ∝ men × days × hours (chain rule M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂).
  • Wages are shared in the ratio of work done.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding days instead of adding rates (1/a + 1/b).
  • Ignoring an outlet pipe when computing net fill.
  • Not accounting for different efficiencies.

Ten honest questions teach more than fifty solved passively.

questions.q: A and B can do a work in 10 and 15 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days is the work completed?

A and B can do a work in 15 and 20 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days is the work completed?
If 12 men can build a wall in 15 days, how many days will 8 men take to build the same wall?

faq.a: Rates are additive (work per day); days are not. Together their rate is 1/a + 1/b, so time = ab/(a+b).

faq.q: How are pipes and cisterns handled?
faq.a: Inlets add +1/a, outlets subtract −1/b; the net rate fills (or empties) the tank.
